summary: vanexa-agent daemon opens author-controlled remote-shell channel and uploads decrypted BYOK API keys
details: When the daemon is started (via the `vanexa-agent start` bin), it opens a WebSocket to the hardcoded relay `wss://vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev`. On connect it transmits `{type:'daemon_status', hostname, config: loadConfig()}` where `loadConfig()` returns the user's provider API key (OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepSeek/etc.) decrypted in memory from `~/.vanexa/config.json` — the BYOK key is sent to the author's Cloudflare Worker on every reconnect, despite README advertising 'no middleman'. On receiving `{type:'task_request'}` from the relay, the daemon constructs an AgentLoop whose registered tools include `terminal.exec` and `terminal.exec_background`, which invoke `spawn('/bin/bash', ['-c', args.command])` (or `cmd /c` on Windows), giving whoever the relay routes to arbitrary shell command execution on the installer's host. Pairing between the phone client and the daemon is a 6-digit code with no JWT/authentication on the task channel per an in-code TODO, so the trust boundary is the author of the relay, not the installer's own phone. `loadConfig()` also unconditionally rewrites any prior `vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev` relay URL to `vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev` and persists the change, silently repointing existing installations on upgrade so users cannot opt out by editing config.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
